title: Role Activation and 90-Day Sponsor Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable, role-based approach for taking a new hire from offer-accept through to independent contributor status by day 90. It emphasizes a sponsor model (an appointed cross-functional peer/manager), concrete activation milestones, manager responsibilities, and integration into Redwood Inference’s performance and feedback cycles.

Goals and scope:
- Reduce time-to-productivity for ICs and managers via standardized activation steps.
- Improve cross-team alignment during onboarding so product, infra, and platform dependencies are resolved within the first 30 days.
- Provide clear manager and sponsor accountabilities to prevent orphaned context.
- Applicable to full-time hires (IC & manager), contractors with >3 month terms, and internal transfers.

Key roles and ownership:
- Hiring Manager (HM): responsible for role outcomes, 1:1 cadence, goal setting, performance calibration, and final signoff on 90-day assessment.
- Sponsor: named peer (not skip-level) who coordinates cross-functional introductions, environment access, and first project scope.
- People Ops (PO): coordinates offer, pre-boarding logistics, and company-level orientation.
- IT/Onboarding Coordinator: creates accounts, hardware provisioning, and access tickets.
- Mentor (optional): technical guide for first 90 days for deeper craft transition.

High-level timeline (offer through day 90):
- Offer -> Day 0 (Pre-boarding, 1–5 business days)
  1. PO sends welcome packet and role activation checklist template.
  2. HM assigns Sponsor & Mentor; Sponsor accepts role in writing.
  3. IT ticket created: laptop, credentials, VPN, email, SSO groups.
  4. Team onboarding calendar seeded (first-week 1:1s, cross-team syncs).

- Day 0 -> Day 7 (First week: orientation & context)
  1. Company orientation (People Ops): culture, benefits, security policy, SLAs for support.
  2. Team onboarding (sponsor-led): tech stack tour, service map, runbook locations, local dev env setup.
  3. First-week objective: successful local build, authenticated access to staging, run a minimal smoke test.

- Day 8 -> Day 30 (Foundational work & impact plan)
  1. HM and hire co-create 30/60/90 OKRs using the included template.
  2. Sponsor facilitates two cross-functional touchpoints to unblock infra/product dependencies.
  3. Goal: deliver a small scoped change or prototype with a documented PR and demo.

- Day 31 -> Day 60 (Ownership & cross-team integration)
  1. Expect increasing velocity on squad tickets; mentor support for architecture/design.
  2. HM runs a 45-day check-in (goals, blockers, career conversation).
  3. Sponsor hands off operational contacts and shift responsibilities for on-call if applicable.

- Day 61 -> Day 90 (Independence & assessment)
  1. HM conducts formal 90-day assessment using the standardized rubric.
  2. If gaps exist, create a targeted development plan (30-day remedy).
  3. Successful activation: owner-level ticket throughput, reliable CI/CD commits, and positive peer feedback.

Activation checklist (required items to complete by day 30):
- Workspace: laptop provisioned, VPN, SSO groups, calendar and Slack access.
- Systems: staging access, service accounts, secrets manager read-only, observability dashboards access.
- Knowledge: README for primary service, architecture diagram viewed, runbooks bookmarked.
- Connections: Sponsor intro calls with product, infra, SRE, and security owners.
- Deliverable: at least one merged PR with test coverage and a demo recorded.

Manager responsibilities (concise list):
1. Assign sponsor and mentor within 48 hours of acceptance.
2. Prepare a focused 30/60/90 objective template prior to day 1.
3. Schedule weekly 1:1s for first 90 days (first four are mandatory).
4. Provide timely feedback after first demo (within 3 business days).
5. Run 90-day calibration with manager’s manager and PO.

Sponsor responsibilities (concise list):
1. Host first-week technical orientation and walkthrough of local dev loop.
2. Book cross-team meetings to introduce service owners and dependencies.
3. Provide two short shadow sessions (pair programming or design review) in the first 30 days.
4. Triage access or escalate to IT/PO when blocked.

90-day assessment rubric (scored per area: 1–5)
- Technical proficiency: understanding of codebase, ability to implement changes.
- Operational readiness: knows deployment path, monitoring, and incident playbooks.
- Collaboration: communicates effectively with cross-functional partners.
- Impact: measurable contributions (tickets, features, bugs fixed).
- Growth mindset: receptivity to feedback and learning cadence.
Scoring guidance: 4–5 means on-track or exceeding expectations; 3 requires close manager coaching; <=2 triggers a performance improvement plan conversation.

Templates and artifacts (copy & adapt):
- 30/60/90 objective template: SMART description, success metrics, dependencies, owner.
- Sponsor acceptance email (one-liner): "I accept the sponsor role for [name], available for 2x 30-mins/week in first month."
- 90-day assessment form: rubric fields and manager comments.
- Offer-to-Day-1 checklist (CSV-ready): role, HM, Sponsor, mentor, laptop request, security training link.

Integration with performance cycles and feedback:
- New hire 90-day assessment results are stored in the employee record and inform the next formal review cycle.
- Managers must incorporate 90-day outcomes into quarterly calibration to align leveling/compensation recommendations.
- Midpoint feedback: HM must provide written feedback at day 45 and record action items in the performance system.

Policy highlights for new hires (quick reference):
- Time off: accrual begins on first payroll; refer to People Ops page for detailed eligibility.
- Security & compliance: complete mandatory security training within first 7 days. Access to production requires completion of production access checklist and manager signoff.
- Remote work: managers may approve full remote arrangements per team policy; ensure onboarding tasks accommodate time zone differences.

Manager escalation and safety net:
- If hire is blocked on critical access for >3 business days, Sponsor escalates to IT lead and copies PO.
- If the HM identifies sustained underperformance between day 45–90, engage People Ops within 5 business days to align next steps (coaching plan, extension, or transition).

Operational metrics (recommend tracking):
- Mean time to first merged PR (target: <=25 days).
- % of hires completing all activation checklist items by day 30 (target: 95%).
- 90-day on-target rate (rubric >=4 aggregate score) (target: 85%).
- Manager satisfaction with onboarding (pulse survey) (target: 4.3/5).

Suggested automation and tooling:
- Populate Offer-to-Day-1 checklist from ATS on offer acceptance to trigger IT and Sponsor assignment.
- Use badge on team dashboards to indicate "Activation Status" (Not started / In progress / Completed).
- Capture 90-day assessment as a structured form in performance system to enable cross-team analytics.

Appendix: sample 30/60/90 objective template (text)
- 30-day: "Understand codebase X; ship initial fix Y; demo to team; measure: merged PR + test coverage >=80%."
- 60-day: "Own feature Z; decrease bug backlog by N%; measure: tickets closed, customer-impacting incidents zeroed."
- 90-day: "Manage small release end-to-end; mentor a new teammate; measure: successful release + peer feedback."

Contact and governance:
- People Ops owners: Aisha Patel (lead), Noah Kim (onboarding ops).
- Manager resource: People Ops manager playbook page (link in related_pages).
- Review cadence: Playbook reviewed annually by People Ops and cross-checked with Eng leadership; next scheduled review Q1 2027.

Notes and change history:
- 2025-09-12: initial draft created.
- 2025-11-04: added sponsor escalation paths and access checklist.
- 2026-02-10: updated metrics and benchmarking targets; published.

End of document.
